steps.description: From the filtered counts, re-estimate size factors and apply variance-stabilizing transformation, keep the 2,000 genes with the highest variance across the 120 samples, and center each gene. Run ConsensusClusterPlus with distance = 1 - Pearson correlation, linkage = ward.D2, reps = 1000, pItem = 0.8, pFeature = 0.8, k = 2:10, fixed seed. Select k from the consensus cumulative distribution function (delta area) and confirm it with the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC) across candidate k; state that delta area alone finds structure in noise. Report the consensus matrix at the chosen k, item-consensus per sample, and cluster-consensus per cluster as the stability estimate. Tabulate the resulting clusters against condition (case/control), library size, and every metadata column, because a cluster explained by depth or a processing variable is technical, not a biological subgroup. Draw the UMAP of the vst values only beside the PCA, as a picture, never as the basis of a cluster or distance claim. Output: chosen k with CDF/delta-area/PAC evidence, consensus matrix heatmap, per-sample cluster assignments with item consensus, per-cluster cluster consensus, cluster x condition and cluster x technical-variable tables, and an explicit stability verdict.

plan.title: Whole-blood subgroups: consensus clustering and stability
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks whether the 120 whole-blood samples (60 case vs 60 control) fall into subgroups beyond the condition split, how many, and how stable. The data are raw gene-level Salmon counts (12,000 genes x 120 samples, single batch), so the plan first characterizes the sample structure on a blind variance-stabilizing transform (QC step: PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to see whether case/control or any technical variable already dominates the primary axes of variance. Low-count genes are then removed with filterByExpr against the condition, and consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus) is run on the variance-stabilized values of the 2,000 most variable genes, centered, with 1-Pearson-correlation distance and ward.D2 linkage: 1,000 resamplings, 80% item subsampling, k from 2 to 10. The number of subgroups k is chosen from the consensus CDF, its delta area, and the proportion of ambiguous clustering (PAC), because delta area alone finds structure in noise; stability is quantified directly by cluster-consensus and item-consensus values. Clusters are tabulated against condition, library size, and available processing variables, since a cluster explained by depth is technical, not biological. The report carries the full reproducibility record. No reference data outside the staged toolchain is needed; the step's grounding names the rules and settings to follow.

ConsensusClusterPlus consensus clustering on vst values, 2000 most variable genes, Pearson correlation distance, ward.D2 linkage
